summary: Trusted verification PASSED (exit code 0): npm install succeeds with expo-sqlite ~57.0.3, typecheck green, 70 tests / 6 suites green, expo export --platform android succeeds, expo prebuild succeeds, Android debug build BUILD SUCCESSFUL. The repair correctly resolves 5 of the 6 previous must-fix findings: (1) package.json pins expo-sqlite ~57.0.3 and package-lock.json now contains the resolved expo-sqlite 57.0.3 entry; (2) the bare '>' in app/index.tsx is now {'>'}; (3) 'tabLabel' was added to the Text Variant union; (4) a real 1024x1024 assets/icon.png exists and prebuild/export resolve all app.json assets; (5) openHousehold now calls setCurrentHouseholdId(id) before router.push('/(tabs)'). The SQLite wiring finding is partially resolved: RepositoryFactory (new) selects SQLite repositories on device with an in-memory fallback, and AppContext now builds repos through createRepositories(), so business data is persisted in the indexed local store. However, two must-fix defects remain. FIRST (regression introduced by the repair): ensureDemoFixture now creates the demo household via create(), which assigns a generated id, while every subsequent fixture record (memberships, members, tasks, entries, todos) and signIn/loadHouseholds still reference the constant DEMO_HOUSEHOLD_ID 'h-core'. loadHouseholds resolves each membership's householdId via getById -> null, so after demo sign-in the root Groups screen shows 'Aucun groupe' and the demo group is unreachable; in the SQLite path the demo user is also created with a generated id so 'demo-user-alex' never exists and duplicate users accumulate on each sign-in. Empirically confirmed with a scratch jest test that mirrors the exact fixture + loadHouseholds logic (loaded.length = 0, expected 1). Additionally reposReady is set but never consumed, so a sign-in before repository init completes skips the fixture and loadHouseholds permanently. SECOND: the required fix verification 'repository tests cover the SQLite-backed repositories' is unmet - __tests__/infrastructure/repositories.test.ts still covers only InMemory repositories and there is zero test coverage for SqliteRepositories or RepositoryFactory. V3-01 domain code is untouched (no diff under src/domain or __tests__/domain) and all previously accepted invariants hold; no chrono/premium/paywall/entitlement behavior and no warm V2 palette were introduced. The delta is coherent and fixable, so the decision is repair (WIP baseline preserved).

findings.problem: Regression introduced by the repair: ensureDemoFixture creates the demo household via repos.households.create() (line 146), which assigns a generated id (e.g. 'household-1-<ts>'), but every subsequent fixture record (memberships lines 157-190, members lines 192-229, tasks/entries/todos lines 231-283) and signIn (line 299) still reference the constant DEMO_HOUSEHOLD_ID 'h-core'. loadHouseholds (lines 309-322) resolves each membership's householdId via households.getById(m.householdId) -> null for 'h-core', so the root Groups screen shows 'Aucun groupe' after demo sign-in and the demo group 'Appartement' is unreachable. The previous baseline seeded the household with id 'h-core' (repos.households.seed([{ id: DEMO_HOUSEHOLD_ID, ... }])) and the fixture was consistent; the repair comment 'For in-memory, set the known ID by updating the created record' has no corresponding code. In the SQLite path the demo user is also created via repos.users.create() (lines 121-141) with a generated id, so 'demo-user-alex' never exists and a duplicate user row is inserted on every sign-in. Additionally reposReady (line 73) is set but never consumed: a sign-in that occurs before repository initialization completes skips ensureDemoFixture and loadHouseholds with no retry, and repos falls back to '{} as AllRepositories' (lines 355-368).
findings.evidence: Scratch jest test in a temp copy mirroring the exact ensureDemoFixture + loadHouseholds logic with in-memory repositories: expect(loaded.length).toBe(1) FAILED with Received: 0 (household 'h-core' not reachable from the user's memberships). git diff --cached shows the seed([{ id: DEMO_HOUSEHOLD_ID, ... }]) call replaced by await repos.households.create({...}) with no id assignment. AppContext.tsx lines 144-155 (create), 157-190 (memberships with DEMO_HOUSEHOLD_ID), 299 (setCurrentHouseholdId(DEMO_HOUSEHOLD_ID)), 315 (getById(m.householdId)).
findings.requiredFix: Keep the demo fixture internally consistent: either seed/create the demo household (and demo user) under the canonical ids (DEMO_HOUSEHOLD_ID 'h-core', 'demo-user-alex') or use the id returned by create() consistently for memberships, members, tasks, entries, todos and currentHouseholdId. Also gate sign-in/loadHouseholds on repository readiness (consume reposReady) or retry the fixture once repos are initialized, so an early sign-in cannot permanently skip the fixture.
